en pølse.explanation: "En pølse" means "a sausage". In Danish, a hot dog is "en hotdog" or "en pølse i brød" (a sausage in bread), and a street stand that sells them is "en pølsevogn" (a hot dog stand).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en varm **pølse** med brød.
sentence.en: I eat a hot sausage with bread.

en pølsevogn.explanation: "En pølsevogn" means "a hot dog stand", a small food wagon on the street that sells hot dogs. It is built from pølse (sausage) and vogn (wagon). "Vogn" is also in "en indkøbsvogn" (a shopping cart) and "en barnevogn" (a stroller).

sentence.da: Hun sælger varme pølser fra en **pølsevogn**.
sentence.en: She sells hot dogs from a hot dog stand.

et palads.explanation: "Et palads" means "a palace", a very large, grand building where a ruler lives. Danish also has "et slot" (a castle), the word used for royal homes like Amalienborg Slot.

sentence.da: Et **palads** har mange store sale og en stor have.
sentence.en: A palace has many big halls and a big garden.

et par.explanation: "Et par" means "a pair" or "a couple", as in "et par sko" (a pair of shoes). It also means "a few": "et par dage" means "a couple of days". Two people in a relationship are also "et par" (a couple).

sentence.da: Jeg bliver her et **par** dage.
sentence.en: I will stay here for a couple of days.

et par jeans.explanation: "Et par jeans" means "a pair of jeans". You can also just say "jeans": "Jeg har jeans på" means "I am wearing jeans".

sentence.da: Jeg køber et **par jeans** i dag.
sentence.en: I am buying a pair of jeans today.

et paradis.explanation: "Et paradis" means "a paradise", a perfect place of happiness. In religion, it is where good people go after death. In everyday speech, it is any wonderful place: "Stranden er et paradis for børn" (The beach is a paradise for children).

sentence.da: Øen er et **paradis** med hvide strande og blåt vand.
sentence.en: The island is a paradise with white beaches and blue water.

et paraplystativ.explanation: "Et paraplystativ" means "an umbrella stand", a holder by the door for wet umbrellas. It is built from paraply (umbrella) and stativ (stand).

sentence.da: Jeg sætter den våde paraply i et **paraplystativ**.
sentence.en: I put the wet umbrella in an umbrella stand.

et parkeringshus.explanation: "Et parkeringshus" means "a parking garage", a building with several floors for cars. It is built from at parkere (to park) and et hus (a house).

sentence.da: Der er ingen pladser på gaden, men der er et **parkeringshus**.
sentence.en: There are no spaces on the street, but there is a parking garage.

et parti.explanation: "Et parti" means "a political party", a group with shared political goals that runs in elections. It also means one game of chess or cards: "Vi spiller et parti skak" (We are playing a game of chess). For a party with food and music, use "en fest" (a party).

sentence.da: Socialdemokratiet er et stort **parti** i Danmark.
sentence.en: The Social Democrats are a big party in Denmark.

et pas.explanation: "Et pas" means "a passport", the document you show at the border. Do not mix it up with "at passe" (to fit, to look after): "Skoen passer" (The shoe fits).

sentence.da: Ved grænsen skal du vise dit **pas**.
sentence.en: At the border you must show your passport.

et pasfoto.explanation: "Et pasfoto" means "a passport photo", a small picture for your passport or ID. It is built from pas (passport) and foto (photo), and "foto" also appears in "et fotoalbum" (a photo album).

sentence.da: Jeg skal bruge et nyt **pasfoto** til mit pas.
sentence.en: I need a new passport photo for my passport.

et penalhus.explanation: "Et penalhus" means "a pencil case", a small case for pens and pencils at school.

sentence.da: Min kuglepen ligger i mit **penalhus**.
sentence.en: My pen is in my pencil case.

et pengeskab.explanation: "Et pengeskab" means "a safe", a strong locked box for money, passports and other valuables. Many hotel rooms have one, and you open it with a code.

sentence.da: Vi gemmer vigtige papirer og smykker i et **pengeskab**.
sentence.en: We keep important papers and jewelry in a safe.

et pensum.explanation: "Et pensum" means "a syllabus", all the material students must learn for a course. Something that will not be tested is "ikke på pensum" (not on the syllabus).

sentence.da: Hele bogen er **pensum**, så vi skal læse den.
sentence.en: The whole book is on the syllabus, so we have to read it.

et personalemøde.explanation: "Et personalemøde" means "a staff meeting", a meeting where everyone who works at a place gathers to share news and decide practical things. The first part, "personale", means the staff.

sentence.da: Alle lærerne mødes til et **personalemøde** hver mandag.
sentence.en: All the teachers meet at a staff meeting every Monday.

et perspektiv.explanation: "Et perspektiv" means "a perspective", a particular way of seeing something: "Det er et interessant perspektiv" (That is an interesting perspective). In drawing, it is also the way lines make a flat picture look deep.

sentence.da: Børn og voksne har ikke det samme **perspektiv** på verden.
sentence.en: Children and adults do not have the same perspective on the world.

et pindsvin.explanation: "Et pindsvin" means "a hedgehog", a small, round animal that sleeps through the winter and often lives in gardens. It is built from the words for stick and hog, so it is literally a stick hog.

sentence.da: Et **pindsvin** har pigge på ryggen og kan rulle sig sammen.
sentence.en: A hedgehog has spines on its back and can roll up into a ball.

et piskeris.explanation: "Et piskeris" means "a whisk", a kitchen tool of wire loops. It is built from at piske (to whip) and ris (twigs).

sentence.da: Jeg rører æg og mel med et **piskeris**.
sentence.en: I mix eggs and flour with a whisk.

et plaster.explanation: "Et plaster" means "a band-aid", a small sticky bandage for a cut.

sentence.da: Sæt et **plaster** på såret.
sentence.en: Put a band-aid on the wound.

et plejebarn.explanation: "Et plejebarn" means "a foster child", a child who lives with another family because the child's own parents cannot look after it. Unlike "et adoptivbarn" (an adopted child), a foster child does not become the legal child of the new family.

sentence.da: Et **plejebarn** bor hos en anden familie, fordi forældrene ikke kan passe det.
sentence.en: A foster child lives with another family because the parents cannot take care of it.

et point.explanation: "Et point" means "a point" in a game or test. A point in a discussion is "en pointe" (a point made in an argument): "Det var en god pointe" (That was a good point).

sentence.da: Vi mangler kun et **point** for at vinde.
sentence.en: We only need one more point to win.

et postbud.explanation: "Et postbud" means "a mail carrier", the person who brings letters to your home. You will also hear "en postmand" (a mailman).

sentence.da: Et **postbud** står ved døren med en pakke.
sentence.en: A mail carrier is at the door with a package.

et posthus.explanation: "Et posthus" means "a post office", the place you go to send and pick up mail. It is built from post (mail) and hus (house).

sentence.da: Jeg skal sende en pakke fra et **posthus**.
sentence.en: I have to send a package from a post office.

et postkontor.explanation: "Et postkontor" means "a post office", where you send letters and packages. It is built from post (mail) and kontor (office). You may also hear "et posthus" (a post office), which means the same.

sentence.da: Jeg sender en pakke på et **postkontor**.
sentence.en: I send a package at a post office.

et postkort.explanation: "Et postkort" means "a postcard", a card you send by mail. It is built from post (mail) and kort (card).

sentence.da: På ferie sender jeg et **postkort** hjem.
sentence.en: On vacation, I send a postcard home.

et postnummer.explanation: "Et postnummer" means "a postal code", the four digits of a Danish address: "2100 København Ø" (2100 Copenhagen Ø). It comes before the town and after the street and house number.

sentence.da: Hvad er dit **postnummer**, så jeg kan sende pakken?
sentence.en: What is your postal code, so I can send the package?

et potentiale.explanation: "Et potentiale" means "a potential", what someone or something could become with time and effort. It is often used without "et": "Der er potentiale i idéen" (There is potential in the idea).

sentence.da: Den unge spiller har et stort **potentiale**, men skal træne mere.
sentence.en: The young player has great potential but needs to train more.

et princip.explanation: "Et princip" means "a principle", a basic belief that guides your decisions. Two set phrases are worth knowing: "af princip" (on principle), as in "Jeg spiser ikke kød af princip" (I do not eat meat on principle), and "i princip" (in principle), as in "I princip kan alle komme" (In principle, anyone can come).

sentence.da: Det er et vigtigt **princip**, at alle får samme chance.
sentence.en: It is an important principle that everyone gets the same chance.

et prisfald.explanation: "Et prisfald" means "a price drop", when something becomes cheaper. It is built from pris (price) and fald (fall).

sentence.da: Efter jul kommer der ofte et **prisfald**.
sentence.en: After Christmas there is often a price drop.

et prisskilt.explanation: "Et prisskilt" means "a price tag", the small sign or label that shows what something costs. It is built from pris (price) and skilt (sign).

sentence.da: Prisen står på et **prisskilt** ved jakken.
sentence.en: The price is on a price tag by the jacket.

et problem.explanation: "Et problem" means "a problem", something difficult that needs to be dealt with. To say "no problem", Danes say "Det er ikke noget problem" (It is no problem).

sentence.da: Vi har et **problem** med bilen.
sentence.en: We have a problem with the car.

et produkt.explanation: "Et produkt" means "a product", something made to be sold. Items on shop shelves are also called "varer" (goods).

sentence.da: Vi sælger et nyt **produkt** i butikken.
sentence.en: We sell a new product in the shop.

et program.explanation: "Et program" means "a program" on a computer. It also means a plan or schedule for an event or a day: "Hvad er programmet i dag?" (What is the plan today?)

sentence.da: Jeg skal installere et nyt **program** på min computer.
sentence.en: I have to install a new program on my computer.

et projekt.explanation: "Et projekt" means "a project", a piece of work with a clear goal and an end: "Vi starter et nyt projekt i dag" (We are starting a new project today).

sentence.da: Vi arbejder på et stort **projekt** sammen.
sentence.en: We are working on a big project together.

et prøverum.explanation: "Et prøverum" means "a fitting room", the little booth in a store, with a curtain or a door, where you check how something fits. It is built from at prøve (to try) and et rum (a room).

sentence.da: Jeg prøver bukserne i et **prøverum**.
sentence.en: I try on the pants in a fitting room.

et pseudonym.explanation: "Et pseudonym" means "a pseudonym", a made-up name that someone uses instead of their real name, often a writer or an artist who wants to stay unknown.

sentence.da: Forfatteren skrev bøgerne under et **pseudonym**, så ingen kendte hendes rigtige navn.
sentence.en: The author wrote the books under a pseudonym, so no one knew her real name.

et pudebetræk.explanation: "Et pudebetræk" means "a pillowcase". It is built from pude (pillow) and betræk (cover), and "betræk" also appears in "et sofabetræk" (a sofa cover).

sentence.da: Jeg putter puden i et **pudebetræk**.
sentence.en: I put the pillow in a pillowcase.

et pulver.explanation: "Et pulver" means "a powder", something dry and fine. It is the second part of "bagepulver" (baking powder).

sentence.da: Rør **pulver** ud i varmt vand.
sentence.en: Stir powder into hot water.

et pund.explanation: "Et pund" means "a pound", both the British money and a weight. In Danish, the weight is 500 grams, which is more than a US pound (454 grams).

sentence.da: Billetten til London koster tyve **pund**.
sentence.en: The ticket to London costs twenty pounds.

et punkt.explanation: "Et punkt" means "a point", a spot or an item on a list. A period at the end of a sentence is "et punktum" (a period).

sentence.da: Det første **punkt** på listen er mælk.
sentence.en: The first item on the list is milk.

et punktum.explanation: "Et punktum" means "a period", the dot at the end of a sentence. Added to a statement, "Punktum!" means "That's final!": "Jeg har sagt nej, punktum!" (I said no, period!)

sentence.da: Der skal være et **punktum** i slutningen af sætningen.
sentence.en: There has to be a period at the end of the sentence.

et puslespil.explanation: "Et puslespil" means "a puzzle", a game where you fit small pieces together into a picture. Do not mix it up with "en gåde" (a riddle), which is a question you solve by thinking.

sentence.da: Et **puslespil** har mange små brikker.
sentence.en: A puzzle has many small pieces.

et påfund.explanation: "Et påfund" means "an idea" and "an invention", something that someone has thought up. It often sounds surprised or critical, as in "Hvad er det for et påfund?" (What kind of idea is that?)

sentence.da: Det er hans eget **påfund**, og ingen andre har prøvet det.
sentence.en: It is his own idea, and nobody else has tried it.

et påskeæg.explanation: "Et påskeæg" means "an Easter egg", often a chocolate egg or a painted egg. It is built from påske (Easter) and æg (egg).

sentence.da: Til påske får jeg et **påskeæg** af chokolade.
sentence.en: At Easter I get an Easter egg made of chocolate.

pandehår.explanation: "Et pandehår" means "bangs", the short hair cut straight across the forehead. Danes say it without "et": "Hun har pandehår" (She has bangs).

sentence.da: Hendes **pandehår** hænger ned over panden og øjnene.
sentence.en: Her bangs hang down over her forehead and eyes.

panik.explanation: "Panik" means "panic", a sudden, overwhelming feeling that makes people stop thinking clearly. Danes say "Jeg var i panik" (I was in a panic), leaving out "a" (literally, "I was in panic").

sentence.da: Der opstod **panik**, da alarmen gik i gang.
sentence.en: Panic broke out when the alarm went off.

pant.explanation: "Pant" means "deposit": a small extra amount added to the price of a bottle or can, which you get back when you return the empty bottle.

forms.en: to return bottles for the deposit

sentence.da: Der er **pant** på flasken.
sentence.en: There is a deposit on the bottle.

pap.explanation: "Pap" means "cardboard", the thick, stiff material boxes are made of. Do not mix it up with "papir" (paper): "pap" is much thicker.

sentence.da: Kassen er lavet af tyk **pap** og er let.
sentence.en: The box is made of thick cardboard and is light.

papir.explanation: "Papir" means "paper", the material you write or print on. In the plural, "papirer" can also mean "documents": "Har du dine papirer med?" (Do you have your papers with you?)

sentence.da: Jeg printer brevet på **papir**.
sentence.en: I print the letter on paper.

paradoksal.explanation: "Paradoksal" means "paradoxical", seeming to contradict itself even though it may still be true.

sentence.da: Situationen er **paradoksal**: Jo mere han sparer, jo mere bruger han.
sentence.en: The situation is paradoxical: the more he saves, the more he spends.

paranoid.explanation: "Paranoid" means "paranoid", believing without reason that others are against you or watching you. Danes also say it as a joke about someone who is too suspicious: "Du er helt paranoid" (You are totally paranoid).

sentence.da: Han er **paranoid** og tror, at naboerne altid holder øje med ham.
sentence.en: He is paranoid and thinks the neighbors are always watching him.

parat.explanation: "Parat" means "ready", prepared to do something. With "stå" (stand) it means being on standby: "Politiet står parat" (The police stand ready).

sentence.da: Er du **parat** til at gå nu?
sentence.en: Are you ready to go now?

parkeret.explanation: "Parkeret" means "parked", for a vehicle that is standing still.

sentence.da: Bilen er **parkeret** foran huset.
sentence.en: The car is parked in front of the house.

parkering.explanation: "Parkering" means "parking", the place where you may leave a car. The action is "at parkere" (to park): "Jeg skal parkere bilen" (I have to park the car).

sentence.da: Der er gratis **parkering** bag ved hotellet.
sentence.en: There is free parking behind the hotel.

parmesan.explanation: "Parmesan" means "parmesan", a hard, salty Italian cheese that is often grated over pasta.

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have lidt **parmesan** på min pasta.
sentence.en: I would like a little parmesan on my pasta.

pas på.explanation: "Pas på" means "watch out" or "be careful": "Pas på, det er varmt" (Careful, it is hot). It also means "look after": "Pas på børnene" (Look after the children).

sentence.da: **Pas på** bilerne!
sentence.en: Watch out for the cars!

pas på dig selv.explanation: "Pas på dig selv" means "take care of yourself" and is a warm way to say goodbye: "Tak for i dag. Pas på dig selv!" (Thanks for today. Take care of yourself!). To several people, say "pas på jer selv" (take care of yourselves).

forms.da: Pas på dig selv i trafikken.

sentence.da: Farvel! **Pas på dig selv**!
sentence.en: Goodbye! Take care of yourself!

passende.explanation: "Passende" means "suitable" or "appropriate": "Det er ikke passende at komme for sent" (It is not appropriate to come late). With a price it means "reasonable": "en passende pris" (a reasonable price).

sentence.da: Jeg leder efter noget **passende** at tage på til festen.
sentence.en: I am looking for something suitable to wear to the party.

passiv.explanation: "Passiv" means "passive", not taking action or joining in. In grammar, a passive sentence tells what happened to something: "Bilen blev stjålet" (The car was stolen).

sentence.da: Hun var **passiv** i timen og sagde aldrig noget.
sentence.en: She was passive in class and never said anything.

pasta.explanation: "Pasta" means "pasta", the Italian food made from wheat dough. You do not use an article with it, so leave out "en": "Jeg laver pasta" (I am making pasta).

sentence.da: Spaghetti er en slags **pasta**.
sentence.en: Spaghetti is a kind of pasta.

peber.explanation: "Peber" means "pepper", the spice you put on food. It is normally used without an article: "Jeg bruger peber på kødet" (I use pepper on the meat). Do not mix it up with "peberfrugt" (bell pepper), which is a vegetable.

sentence.da: Jeg tilføjer lidt salt og **peber**.
sentence.en: I add a little salt and pepper.

penge.explanation: "Penge" means "money". You do not use an article with it: "Jeg har ingen penge" (I have no money). For one coin or one note, say "en mønt" (a coin) or "en seddel" (a banknote).

sentence.da: Man betaler med **penge**.
sentence.en: You pay with money.

pensioneret.explanation: "Pensioneret" means "retired", no longer working because of age.

sentence.da: Min far er **pensioneret** og har meget tid.
sentence.en: My father is retired and has a lot of time.

perfekt.explanation: "Perfekt" means "perfect". As a reply, "Perfekt!" means "Great, that works!".

sentence.da: Et **perfekt** svar har ingen fejl.
sentence.en: A perfect answer has no mistakes.

permanent.explanation: "Permanent" means "permanent", meant to stay for good, not just for a while. The opposite is "midlertidig" (temporary).

sentence.da: Han har et **permanent** job i en bank.
sentence.en: He has a permanent job at a bank.

persille.explanation: "Persille" means "parsley", a green herb often sprinkled on food at the end.

sentence.da: Jeg drysser frisk **persille** på kartoflerne.
sentence.en: I sprinkle fresh parsley on the potatoes.

personale.explanation: "Et personale" means "staff", all the people who work at a shop, hospital or company. For one person, say "en medarbejder" (an employee).

sentence.da: Sygeplejersker og læger er en del af hospitalets **personale**.
sentence.en: Nurses and doctors are part of the hospital's staff.

personlig.explanation: "Personlig" means "personal", belonging to one person's own life or character: "Det er et personligt spørgsmål" (That is a personal question). It also means "with your own character": "en personlig stil" (a personal style).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **personlig** mening om det.
sentence.en: I have a personal opinion about it.

personligt.explanation: "Personligt" means "personally" and starts a sentence with your own opinion: "Personligt kan jeg godt lide vinteren" (Personally, I like winter). It also means "in person": "Jeg har mødt hende personligt" (I have met her in person).

sentence.da: **Personligt** kan jeg godt lide den nye film.
sentence.en: Personally, I like the new movie.

pervers.explanation: "Pervers" means "perverted", a strong, negative word for behavior seen as sick or morally wrong, often sexual. It can also mean "perverse", against what is reasonable: "Det er pervers, at ..." (It is perverse that ...).

sentence.da: Hans humor er **pervers**, og folk bliver ofte stødt.
sentence.en: His humor is perverted, and people are often offended.

pessimistisk.explanation: "Pessimistisk" means "pessimistic", expecting things to go badly. Say it about a person, "Hun er pessimistisk" (She is pessimistic), or about a view, such as "en pessimistisk prognose" (a pessimistic forecast).

sentence.da: Han er **pessimistisk** og tror altid, at det går galt.
sentence.en: He is pessimistic and always thinks it will go wrong.

pinlig.explanation: "Pinlig" means "embarrassing" and describes the situation. To describe your own feeling, say "Jeg er flov" (I am embarrassed).

sentence.da: Den situation var meget **pinlig**.
sentence.en: That situation was very embarrassing.

pinse.explanation: "En pinse" means "Pentecost" or "Whitsun", a church holiday seven weeks after Easter. In Denmark "pinsedag" (Whit Sunday) and "anden pinsedag" (Whit Monday) are days off, so it is a long weekend.

sentence.da: Til **pinse** er der en ekstra fridag om mandagen.
sentence.en: At Pentecost there is an extra day off on Monday.

piskefløde.explanation: "Piskefløde" means "whipping cream", cream with enough fat that you can whip it. It is built from at piske (to whip) and fløde (cream). Cream for coffee is called "kaffefløde" (coffee cream).

forms.en: The cake has whipping cream in it.

sentence.da: Vi pisker **piskefløde** til kagen.
sentence.en: We whip whipping cream for the cake.

pjat.explanation: "Pjat" means "nonsense". Use it to wave off an idea: "Han taler pjat" (He is talking nonsense). As a quick reply, "Pjat!" is a light way to say you do not believe it.

sentence.da: Det er noget **pjat**, og jeg tror ikke på det.
sentence.en: That is nonsense, and I don't believe it.

placeret.explanation: "Placeret" means "placed" or "located": "Hotellet er placeret tæt på stationen" (The hotel is located close to the station). With "højt" (high) it also means high-ranking: "en højt placeret politiker" (a high-ranking politician).

sentence.da: Skolen er **placeret** midt i byen, tæt på stationen.
sentence.en: The school is located in the middle of town, close to the station.

pladsmangel.explanation: "En pladsmangel" means "lack of space", not enough room for people or things. Danish often builds words like this with "mangel" (lack) on the end, for example "vandmangel" (lack of water).

forms.en: lack of space in the apartment

sentence.da: Der er **pladsmangel** i garagen, og der kan ikke stå flere biler.
sentence.en: There is a lack of space in the garage, and no more cars can fit.

planlægning.explanation: "Planlægning" means "planning", deciding in advance what to do and when. Do not mix it up with "en plan" (a plan): "planlægning" is the work of making plans, while "en plan" is the finished plan: "Vi har en plan" (We have a plan).

sentence.da: Før festen er der meget **planlægning**.
sentence.en: Before the party there is a lot of planning.

plastik.explanation: "Plastik" means "plastic". Many words start with it, such as "plastikaffald" (plastic waste).

sentence.da: Flasken er lavet af **plastik**, ikke glas.
sentence.en: The bottle is made of plastic, not glass.

plastikaffald.explanation: "Plastikaffald" means "plastic waste", trash made of plastic such as bottles and bags. Danish builds many words from a material plus "affald" (waste), such as "madaffald" (food waste).

sentence.da: Tomme flasker og poser af plastik er **plastikaffald**.
sentence.en: Empty bottles and bags made of plastic are plastic waste.

plat.explanation: "Plat" means "vulgar" or "cheesy", for jokes, remarks and entertainment that feel crude or cheap.

sentence.da: Hans humor er **plat**, og kun få griner af den.
sentence.en: His humor is cheesy, and few people laugh at it.

pleje.explanation: "En pleje" means "care", looking after someone who is sick or old, or after your body. It is practical care, unlike "omsorg" (warm concern). The verb "at pleje" also means "to usually do something": "Jeg plejer at stå tidligt op" (I usually get up early).

sentence.da: På sygehuset arbejder hun med **pleje** af syge.
sentence.en: At the hospital she works caring for sick people.

pludselig.explanation: "Pludselig" means "suddenly" or "sudden". Before a noun it means "sudden": "en pludselig lyd" (a sudden sound). At the start of a sentence it means "suddenly", and the verb comes right after it: "Pludselig kom han ind" (Suddenly he came in).

sentence.da: **Pludselig** hørte jeg et højt brag.
sentence.en: Suddenly I heard a loud bang.

poesi.explanation: "En poesi" means "poetry", written art that plays with sound and images. It can describe a beautiful, dreamlike quality in something: "Der er poesi i den gamle by" (There is poetry in the old town).

sentence.da: I **poesi** står ordene ofte i korte linjer og med rim.
sentence.en: In poetry the words are often in short lines and with rhyme.

polen.explanation: "Polen" means "Poland". Use "i" (in) for being there and "til" (to) for going there: "Vi rejser til Polen" (We are traveling to Poland).

sentence.da: Warszawa ligger i **Polen**.
sentence.en: Warsaw is in Poland.

politi.explanation: "Politi" means "police". Leave out "en" before it, and add "-et" for "the police": "Politiet er her" (The police are here). One officer is "en politibetjent" (a police officer).

sentence.da: **Politi** og ambulance er kommet.
sentence.en: The police and an ambulance have arrived.

politisk.explanation: "Politisk" means "political". Use it for debates and decisions about running a country: "en politisk debat" (a political debate). The subject itself is "politik" (politics).

sentence.da: Det er en **politisk** beslutning, ikke min.
sentence.en: It is a political decision, not mine.

polsk.explanation: "Polsk" means "Polish", for things from Poland and for the language. Danish writes languages and nationalities with a lowercase letter, so "polsk" is not capitalized.

sentence.da: Min nabo kommer fra Polen og taler **polsk**.
sentence.en: My neighbor comes from Poland and speaks Polish.

polyester.explanation: "En polyester" means "polyester", a man-made fabric used for clothes and sports gear. It dries quickly and does not wrinkle easily.

sentence.da: Mærket i trøjen viser, at den er lavet af **polyester**.
sentence.en: The label in the sweater shows that it is made of polyester.

pommes frites.explanation: "Pommes frites" means "French fries". Danes often shorten it to "pommes" (fries).

sentence.da: **Pommes frites** er lavet af kartofler.
sentence.en: French fries are made of potatoes.

popcorn.explanation: "Popcorn" means "popcorn" and is spelled as in English. To indicate an amount, name the container that holds the popcorn: "en spand popcorn" (a bucket of popcorn).

sentence.da: Jeg køber **popcorn**, før filmen starter.
sentence.en: I buy popcorn before the movie starts.

populær.explanation: "Populær" means "popular", for people, places and things that many people enjoy.

sentence.da: Det er en **populær** café, så vi bestiller bord.
sentence.en: It is a popular café, so we are booking a table.

porcelæn.explanation: "Porcelæn" means "china" or "porcelain", a fine, hard ceramic used for plates, cups and vases. Danes also use it for the dishes themselves: "det fine porcelæn" (the good china).

sentence.da: Tallerkener og kopper af **porcelæn** går let i stykker.
sentence.en: Plates and cups made of porcelain break easily.

porto.explanation: "Porto" means "postage", the price for sending a letter or package: "Hvad koster porto til Tyskland?" (What does postage to Germany cost?)

sentence.da: Hvor meget er **porto** til et brev til Tyskland?
sentence.en: How much is postage for a letter to Germany?

positiv.explanation: "Positiv" means "positive", both for things and for people: "positive nyheder" (positive news), "Hun er meget positiv" (She is very upbeat). The opposite is "negativ" (negative).

sentence.da: Han har en meget **positiv** holdning.
sentence.en: He has a very positive attitude.

positivt.explanation: "Positivt" means "positively", in a good or hopeful way: "Hun svarede positivt" (She answered positively). It often follows "tænke" (think) and "reagere" (react): "Tænk positivt!" (Think positively!)

sentence.da: Chefen reagerede **positivt** på forslaget og sagde ja.
sentence.en: The boss reacted positively to the proposal and said yes.

post.explanation: "Post" means "mail": the letters and parcels that arrive. You say it without "en": "Jeg har fået post" (I have received mail).

sentence.da: Postbuddet kommer hver dag med **post** til os.
sentence.en: The mail carrier comes every day with mail for us.

pragtfuld.explanation: "Pragtfuld" means "splendid": magnificent and beautiful, such as a view, a building or a sunset: "en pragtfuld udsigt" (a splendid view). It is built from pragt (splendor) and -fuld (full of).

sentence.da: Fra tårnet er udsigten over byen og havet **pragtfuld**.
sentence.en: From the tower, the view over the city and the sea is splendid.

praktisk.explanation: "Praktisk" means "practical" and "handy", for things that are useful in daily life. About a person, it means good with your hands: "Jeg er ikke så praktisk" (I am not very handy).

sentence.da: Den lille taske er meget **praktisk** på ture.
sentence.en: The small bag is very practical on trips.

pressefrihed.explanation: "Pressefrihed" means "freedom of the press", the right of the media and reporters to publish what they find without government control.

forms.en: freedom of the press in Denmark

sentence.da: Med **pressefrihed** må journalister skrive om politikerne uden at blive straffet.
sentence.en: With freedom of the press, journalists may write about the politicians without being punished.
